Patañjali
grammarian. said to be the son of Goṇikā; traditionally considered to be a. incarnation of serpent Ādiśeṣa an. identical with Caraka an. a. of Yogasūtra; prob. a contemporary of Puṣyamitra. For discussions of his date a. 175 B. C. to 280 A. D. see Belvalkar, Systems of Skt. Gr. p.. 32-33; Y. Mimamsak, Sam3s. Vyākaraṇ Śāstra kā Itihās I. p.. 315, 318-28; [Page090-a. S. D. Joshi an. J. A. F. Roodbergen, Patañjali's Vyākaraṇa Mahābhāṣya Intro. p.. 1-34; G. Cardona, Pāṇini, A Survey of Research, p.. 263-6; K. V. Abhyankar, Dict. of Skt. Gr. p.. 215-16. ABORI. (Diamond Jubilee Vol.) 58 an. 59 (1978) p.. 79-99.
On the relationship between Patañjali an. Kātyāyana, see under Kātyāyana, NCC. III. p. 321b; also G. Cardona, op. cit. p. 260.
For a study on Patañjali's Mahābhāṣya, see Theosophist X. p.. 724-40; IHQ. 2. p.. 67-76, 262-89, 464-94, 738-60; B. N. Puri, India in the time of Patañjali. Bombay, 1968.
On his nativity see Cardona, op. cit. p.. 269-70.
For a legendary account of his life see Patañjalicarita in Skt. below.
-- Mahābhāṣya, elaborate commentorial exposition of Aṣṭādhyāyī of Pāṇini an. Vārttikas of Kātyāyana.
Pt.. (1) F. Kielhorn. Bomb. Skt. Ser. in 3 pts. 1st edn. 1880. 1883. 1885; 2nd edn. 1892. 1906. 1909; 3rd revised edn. K. V. Abhyankar. BORI. Poona, 1962. (2) N. S. Press. Bombay, 1917.

Pātimokkha
or Prā(a)timokṣa sūtras. Bud. Pāli an. Skt. formed nucleus of Vinayapiṭaka; is a list of transgressions an. their atonements: Pāli text appears to belong to Theravādins, an. Skt. text to the Sarvāstivādins; present text compiled about 1st Cent. B. C.; Chinese an. Tibetan translations also available; rules vary in diff. texts belonging to diff. schools.
